chunks: Al-Husayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Muʿadhi, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Layth, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from Abi Bashir, from Hafsah bint Sirin, from Umm Sulayman, from the mother of Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said:

When a woman dies and they intend to wash her, then let them begin with her abdomen, and let it be wiped with a gentle wiping if she is not pregnant. But if she is pregnant, then do not move her. Then when you intend to perform her ghusl, begin with her lower parts, and place over her ʿawrah a concealing cloth. Then take a piece of cotton and wash her, then insert your hand from beneath the cloth and wash her with cotton three times, and do well in wiping her before performing wudu (ablution) for her. Then perform wudu (ablution) for her with water in which lotus leaves have been placed, and he mentioned the hadith.

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman; the deceased female subject of the ruling
key_terms.تُوَضِّئِيهَا: you perform wudu (ablution) for her; the pre-ghusl ablution mentioned in the report
key_terms.تُوُفِّيَتِ: she passed away; indicates the death of the woman whose body is to be prepared
key_terms.ثَوْبًا سَتِيرًا: a concealing cloth; a covering used to preserve modesty during washing
key_terms.حُبْلَى: pregnant; specifies a condition affecting how the body is handled
key_terms.سِدْرٌ: lotus leaves; used in the water for washing the deceased
key_terms.عَوْرَتِهَا: her ʿawrah; the area that must be covered from view
key_terms.غُسْلَهَا: her ghusl (ritual washing); the funerary washing of the deceased

ai.seo_question: How should the body of a deceased woman be prepared and washed according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal instructions for preparing the body of a deceased woman for ghusl, including modesty, gentleness, and the order of washing. It emphasizes care for the deceased, especially in the case of pregnancy, and mentions performing wudu (ablution) before the full washing.
